Class AbstractOutputFile

java.lang.Object
dev.hardwood.AbstractOutputFile
All Implemented Interfaces:
OutputFile, Closeable, AutoCloseable
Direct Known Subclasses:
InMemoryOutputFile, S3OutputFile
@Experimental public abstract class AbstractOutputFile extends Object implements OutputFile

A base for implementing OutputFile that enforces its lifecycle.

The public methods are final: each checks the state the lifecycle table in OutputFile allows it in, throws IllegalStateException otherwise, and calls the protected do method that does the work. position() counts the bytes doWrite(ByteBuffer) accepted. A subclass implements doWrite and overrides the others it needs; they do nothing by default:

Method Called by, while the file is open Does
doCreate() create() acquires the destination's resources
doWrite(ByteBuffer) write appends the bytes
doClose() close() publishes the file at the destination
doDiscard() discard(), or close() when doClose() throws releases the resources and throws away what was written

Each do method other than doWrite is called at most once per file. When doCreate() throws, the file ends discarded without a call to doDiscard(), so doCreate() must leave nothing held when it fails. When doClose() throws, the file ends discarded: doDiscard() runs, a failure of it is attached to the doClose() failure as suppressed, and the doClose() failure is rethrown. The file is discarded before doDiscard() runs and is not discarded again, so doDiscard() must release what it can before it throws.

This API is Experimental: the shape may change in future releases.

      protected void doClose() throws IOException
      Publishes the file at the destination. May leave resources held when it fails, for doDiscard() to release. Does nothing by default.

      IOException - if the file cannot be published; the file then ends discarded

    • doDiscard

      protected void doDiscard() throws IOException
      Releases the resources and throws away what was written, leaving the destination as if nothing was written. Releases what it can before it throws, since it is not called again. Does nothing by default.

      IOException - if the resources cannot be released
